A seed is a small object produced by a plant, from which a new plant of the same kind can grow.

Think of a sunflower seed, a mango seed (the pit), or a tiny mustard seed. Each one is essentially a package — it contains a miniature, undeveloped plant (called an embryo) wrapped in stored food to nourish it and protected by a hard outer coat. Everything that plant needs to get its life started is packed inside that tiny object.

A seed doesn't start growing the moment it exists. It stays dormant — almost "asleep" — waiting for the right conditions: enough moisture, the right temperature, and often soil. When those conditions arrive, it germinates, meaning it cracks open, sends a root downward, and pushes a shoot upward. That's the moment the seed fulfills its purpose. A single seed can eventually grow into an enormous oak tree, a field of wheat, or a garden of flowers.

This core meaning — a small thing that holds the potential for something much larger — is so powerful that it has spread into almost every area of human life and language.
The Figurative Meaning: The Beginning of Something

Because a real seed is the origin of a living plant, the word "seed" is very widely used to mean the first, small beginning of something that will grow over time.

"The seeds of doubt were planted in her mind."

This means doubt started — in a small way — and would likely grow.

"That one conversation was the seed of a great friendship."
"The protests were the seed of a revolution."
"His boredom in that hospital bed became the seed of his greatest invention."

Whenever something starts small and quietly — an idea, an emotion, a conflict, a movement — and later grows into something significant, we often say the "seed" of it was there at the beginning. You'll encounter this usage constantly in books, speeches, journalism, and everyday conversation.
The Literary and Biblical Meaning: Offspring and Descendants

In older English, formal writing, and especially religious or biblical texts, "seed" refers to a person's children, grandchildren, and all the descendants that follow them — essentially, the living continuation of someone's bloodline.

"He promised that the land would belong to his seed forever."
"She was of the seed of David."

This meaning is rare in everyday modern speech, but you'll come across it when reading older literature, the Bible, or historical texts. When you see it used this way, it simply means the people who came from someone — their biological legacy stretching through generations.
The Sports Meaning: A Ranked Competitor

In competitive tournaments — especially in tennis, chess, squash, and many other sports — a seed is a player or team that has been officially ranked and placed in a specific position within a tournament bracket.

The purpose of seeding is fairness in competition: if you just drew names randomly, the two best players in the world might end up facing each other in the very first round, eliminating one great player immediately. To prevent this, organizers rank the best players as the "1st seed," "2nd seed," "3rd seed," and so on, and arrange the bracket so the strongest players are kept apart until the later rounds.

"She is the top seed at the French Open this year." (She is ranked #1 in this tournament.)
"The 3rd seed was knocked out in the quarterfinals."
"He was unseeded — nobody expected him to reach the final."

Being "seeded" means you are officially recognized as one of the stronger competitors. The number tells you how strong: the 1st seed (also called the "top seed") is considered the best, the 2nd seed the second-best, and so on. When a lower-ranked player beats a higher-ranked one, it's called an "upset."

In the world of startups and business, a seed (or seed round / seed funding) refers to the very first investment that a new company receives to get started.

Just as a plant seed is the beginning before anything has grown, seed funding is the earliest money a business idea receives — before the company has proven itself, before it has significant customers or revenue.

"The startup raised $1.5 million in a seed round."
"He's looking for seed capital to build his first prototype."

Investors who put money in at this stage are called "seed investors." It's considered a high-risk investment because the business is still just an idea or in its earliest form — like betting on a seed before you know if it'll grow.
The Computing Meaning: A Starting Value for Randomness

In computer science and mathematics, a seed (also called a random seed or seed value) is a starting number given to an algorithm that generates a sequence of seemingly random numbers.

Here's why this matters: computers don't generate truly random numbers — they use mathematical formulas that look random. If you give the formula a starting number (the seed), it will produce a specific sequence every single time you use that same starting number. If you change the seed, you get a completely different sequence.

"Set the random seed to 42 so the experiment can be reproduced."
"The simulation uses a seed to ensure consistent results across tests."

This is enormously useful in science, gaming, and software testing — if you want someone else to be able to reproduce your exact results, you share the seed you used. In video games like Minecraft, a "seed" determines the entire randomly-generated world — share that seed with someone else, and they get the exact same world.
The Weather Science Meaning: Cloud Seeding

In meteorology, cloud seeding is a technique where tiny particles (such as silver iodide or dry ice) are released into clouds to encourage rain or snow to form.

In nature, water droplets in clouds need something to form around — a tiny particle of dust, salt, or pollen. When clouds don't have enough of these natural particles, they may hold moisture without releasing it as rain. Scientists artificially introduce particles — the "seeds" — to give the water droplets something to form around, triggering rainfall.

"The government used cloud seeding to try to end the drought."
"Several countries now use cloud seeding to increase rainfall in dry regions."

The particles are the seeds: small, introduced things that make something much larger (a rainstorm) begin.

The word "seed" carries one powerful, unifying idea across all its uses: something small that is the starting point for something larger. Whether it's a literal plant seed, the seed of an idea, a seeded tennis player placed strategically at the start of a tournament, the first investment in a company, or a starting value that generates an entire sequence — in every case, the seed is the origin, the trigger, the first cause of everything that follows.

That's why it's such a rich and widely-used word: the image of a tiny seed growing into something vast is one of the most universal ideas in human experience.
